Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Communications Engineering and 16 years of software development experience in the biotechnology industry, my research perspective is deeply influenced by my technical and strategic background. My 12 years of Scrum experience guide me to focus on frameworks and definitions of software quality relevant to practitioners. This background may lead me to prioritize structured methods over flexible interpretations, potentially biasing my assumptions towards the effectiveness of current industry practices. Consequently, my analytical decisions and interpretation of how Scrum practitioners define software quality may emphasize efficiency and alignment with established methodologies, affecting the coding and thematic outcomes of my analysis.

init_codebook.definition: Quality encompasses both the software product and the development process used to create it.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions quality as both a process and a product.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions only product quality or process quality separately.
typical_examples: Software quality is both outcome and process.
atypical_examples: Quality can be defined in many ways.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Relates to how practitioners view software quality as a holistic concept involving both product and process aspects.

init_codebook.definition: Quality related to the internal attributes of the software, such as code cleanliness and design sustainability.
inclusion_criteria: References internal aspects such as code quality or sustainable design.
exclusion_criteria: Focuses solely on external factors like meeting business needs or defect-free operation.
typical_examples: Internal quality has to do with the way that the system has been built and designed.
atypical_examples: For me, Agile brings two perspectives to quality, the process quality and the structural quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights the importance of internal software attributes in defining software quality.

init_codebook.definition: An iterative process of enhancing both the software and the processes by reflecting and adapting.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions continuous improvement or learning within software development.
exclusion_criteria: Does not mention iteration or adjustment over time.
typical_examples: The process is always subject to improvements.
atypical_examples: I’m glad this is not an exam question!
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows how practitioners value iterative enhancement as a core part of quality.

init_codebook.definition: The concept of software quality is perceived differently and can't be objectively defined as one singular element.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions the subjective nature of defining software quality.
exclusion_criteria: Attempts to propose objective metrics or definitions for quality.
typical_examples: It is a challenging question because quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: Agile advocates for quality but it doesn’t necessarily define it.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Reflects the difficulty in establishing a universal definition among practitioners.

init_codebook.definition: Quality attributes that are observable by end-users and stakeholders, such as defect-free performance and meeting business needs.
inclusion_criteria: Focus is on quality of the final product or its adherence to user needs.
exclusion_criteria: Focus is solely on internal quality aspects like code cleanliness.
typical_examples: Software quality is first and most the product confirms to the requirements and free of defects.
atypical_examples: In agile, we also keen on creating software design that is sustainable.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Clarifies how practitioners evaluate quality based on user-facing characteristics.

init_codebook.definition: Agile practices are seen as integral to achieving and maintaining software quality through frameworks and methodologies.
inclusion_criteria: Agile or Scrum is mentioned as a means to enhance software quality.
exclusion_criteria: Does not reference Agile or focuses only on traditional methods.
typical_examples: Agile calls for delivering a working software frequently.
atypical_examples: Software quality can be defined as the ability of the software to function as per user requirements and of course no defects.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows the perceived impact of Agile methodologies on software quality from the practitioner's perspective.

Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Communications Engineering and 16 years of experience in biotechnology and software development, including 12 years with Scrum, my background deeply influences my research perspective on how Scrum practitioners define software quality. My technical and industry-specific knowledge may lead me to prioritize functional and technical aspects over user-centered issues. I might assume that software quality inherently aligns with engineering standards, which could bias my interpretation of qualitative data towards a technical lens. This positionality could shape how I code and interpret responses, potentially overemphasizing engineering precision and undervaluing softer, team-oriented aspects critical in Scrum development environments.

init_codebook.definition: The quality of software encompasses both the development process and the final product.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of quality related to the development process and the final product
exclusion_criteria: Focus solely on either product or process quality without mentioning both
typical_examples: Software quality is both outcome and process.
atypical_examples: Quality take place in many aspects of what we do in software development.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explains how practitioners view quality as a combination of process and product outcomes.

init_codebook.definition: Software quality is defined by how well it meets business or user needs.
inclusion_criteria: References to software meeting business or user needs as a measure of quality
exclusion_criteria: Mentions of technical aspects of quality without reference to business needs
typical_examples: Software quality is the end result. It has a structural perspective which is the code and the design. It has also an external component which is free of defects and meets the end user requirements.
atypical_examples: Quality can be defined in many ways. The definition may differ from person to person.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights how quality is assessed by the alignment of software with business goals.

init_codebook.definition: Focus on the internal attributes of software like clean code and sustainable design.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of clean code, sustainable design, or technical internal quality
exclusion_criteria: Discusses only external or end-user features without internal technical focus
typical_examples: Yes, very important question! Software quality is first and most the product confirms to the requirements and free of defects.
atypical_examples: We need the whole hour just for this question!
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Emphasizes technical aspects that practitioners consider vital for software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Quality is recognized as a subjective concept that is complex and difficult to define.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of complexity or subjectivity in defining software quality
exclusion_criteria: Concrete or singular definitions of quality without mention of complexity
typical_examples: It is a challenging question, because quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: Agile came in with a purpose to improve software quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Acknowledges challenges in arriving at a common definition of software quality.

init_codebook.definition: The process of consistently improving practices and products to enhance quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of continuous improvement or reflection as a means to enhance quality
exclusion_criteria: Static or one-time improvement methods without ongoing refinement
typical_examples: The agile process itself is subject to continuous improvements.
atypical_examples: In agile, we believe in responding to change over following a plan.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Illustrates how continuous improvement practices contribute to the perception of quality.

Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Communications Engineering and 16 years in biotechnology and software development, my research on how Scrum practitioners define software quality is shaped by my technical and leadership expertise. My experience over 12 years in Scrum could lead to a bias toward frameworks that emphasize efficiency and innovation, potentially skewing my interpretation toward these dimensions. I might assume that software quality naturally aligns with technical specifications, affecting my coding choices. My background could inadvertently prioritize quantitative measures over more subjective quality indicators, which may influence data analysis outcomes.

init_codebook.code: Software Quality at Process and Product Level
init_codebook.definition: Quality is defined at both the process and software levels.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions quality at both the process and software levels.
exclusion_criteria: Focuses solely on one level, either process or software.
typical_examples: But for the purpose of a definition, I would say quality takes place in the process level and the software level.
atypical_examples: Quality can be defined in many ways. The definition may differ from person to person.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: It explains the dual perspective of defining software quality in Scrum practice.

init_codebook.definition: Implementation of practices during software development assures quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions practices implemented during development.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses results without mentioning practices.
typical_examples: During the software development process, we implement and exercise practices that assure quality.
atypical_examples: The agile process itself is subject to continuous improvements.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights specific practices Scrum practitioners use to achieve quality.

init_codebook.code: Conformity and Defect Free as Quality Attributes
init_codebook.definition: Key attributes of software include conformity to business needs and being free of defects.
inclusion_criteria: Notes conformity to business needs and freedom from defects.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions only one of the attributes, either conformity or defect-free.
typical_examples: For the software or the end product, I believe the key attributes is conformity to business needs and free of defects.
atypical_examples: Yes. Good question. The process is the software development method and its principles and guidelines we use to deliver the software.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Directly addresses how Scrum practitioners define quality characteristics.

init_codebook.definition: Internal quality encompasses maintainability, understanding, and reusability of code.
inclusion_criteria: Focuses on internal aspects like maintainability, understanding, reusability.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions external quality or defect-free aspects only.
typical_examples: We have to add the desires to maintain, understand and reuse code to evaluate quality.
atypical_examples: Software quality is an abstract and complex concept.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explains internal attributes that are valued by Scrum practitioners in defining quality.

init_codebook.definition: Using retrospectives to continuously reflect and improve the process to deliver quality software.
inclusion_criteria: Discusses the role of continuous improvement in process.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses quality without mentioning improvement or retrospectives.
typical_examples: We use retrospectives to continuously reflect on the way we work to become better at what we do and ultimately better at delivering quality software.
atypical_examples: Very subjective and it depends on who you ask.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Illustrates the value of process improvement in defining quality for Scrum practitioners.

init_codebook.definition: Agile shifts focus toward code quality and adaptive design.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions Agile's impact on quality focus, especially on code and design.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses Agile without relation to quality focus.
typical_examples: There was a great focus on product level quality. Mainly free of defects and meets customer’s needs. I saw in agile a shift toward code quality and a design that responds to change.
atypical_examples: Quality can be defined in many ways.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Provides insight into how Agile practices alter the definition of quality in Scrum.

init_codebook.definition: Quality in Agile requires clean, readable, and maintainable code.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions clean, readable, maintainable code as a sign of quality.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses code without aspects of cleanliness or maintainability.
typical_examples: Clean code is subjective, but we know at least it should be simple, readable and maintainable.
atypical_examples: You cannot test correctness into a program.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Clarifies how specific characteristics of code contribute to the definition of quality.

init_codebook.code: User Satisfaction and Fit for Purpose
init_codebook.definition: Software must fit its purpose and meet user needs for quality.
inclusion_criteria: Emphasizes meeting user needs and fitting the purpose as quality indicators.
exclusion_criteria: Only talks about defect-free aspects.
typical_examples: Software quality means first and foremost no bugs. The business doesn’t like buggy software.
atypical_examples: Software quality is subjective, but we always know it when we see it.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Details the user-centric view of software quality among practitioners.

codebook.definition: Quality encompasses both the software product and the development process used to create it.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions quality as both a process and a product.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions only product quality or process quality separately.
typical_examples: Software quality is both outcome and process.
atypical_examples: Quality can be defined in many ways.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Relates to how practitioners view software quality as a holistic concept involving both product and process aspects.
codebook.notes: Aligned from codes 'Software Quality at Process and Product Level' and 'Quality as Process and Product'. This was supported by Reviewer-Agent agreements, showing strong conceptual overlap.

codebook.definition: An iterative process of enhancing both the software and the processes by reflecting and adapting.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions continuous improvement or learning within software development.
exclusion_criteria: Does not mention iteration or adjustment over time.
typical_examples: The process is always subject to improvements.
atypical_examples: I’m glad this is not an exam question!
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows how practitioners value iterative enhancement as a core part of quality.
codebook.notes: Retained based on Reviewer-Agent agreements and consistent definition across sources.

codebook.definition: Quality related to the internal attributes of the software, such as code cleanliness and design sustainability.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions internal aspects like maintainability, understanding, reusability.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses only external or end-user features without internal technical focus.
typical_examples: Internal quality has to do with the way that the system has been built and designed.
atypical_examples: We need the whole hour just for this question!
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights the importance of internal software attributes in defining software quality.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'Internal_Quality' and 'Clean and Maintainable Code'. Justified by Reviewer-Agent consensus on internal quality attributes.

codebook.definition: The concept of software quality is perceived differently and can't be objectively defined as one singular element.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions the subjective nature of defining software quality.
exclusion_criteria: Attempts to propose objective metrics or definitions for quality.
typical_examples: It is a challenging question because quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: Agile advocates for quality but it doesn’t necessarily define it.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Reflects the difficulty in establishing a universal definition among practitioners.
codebook.notes: Retained based on Discussion-Agent's support of subjectivity in quality definition. Supported by literature.

codebook.definition: Quality attributes that are observable by end-users and stakeholders, such as defect-free performance and meeting business needs.
inclusion_criteria: Focus is on quality of the final product or its adherence to user needs.
exclusion_criteria: Focus is solely on internal quality aspects like code cleanliness.
typical_examples: Software quality is first and most the product confirms to the requirements and free of defects.
atypical_examples: In agile, we also keen on creating software design that is sustainable.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Clarifies how practitioners evaluate quality based on user-facing characteristics.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'External Quality' and 'Conformance to Business Needs'. Retained after considering the Discussion-Agent's focus on technical and strategic alignment.

codebook.definition: Agile practices are seen as integral to achieving and maintaining software quality through frameworks and methodologies.
inclusion_criteria: Agile or Scrum is mentioned as a means to enhance software quality.
exclusion_criteria: Does not reference Agile or focuses only on traditional methods.
typical_examples: Agile calls for delivering a working software frequently.
atypical_examples: Software quality can be defined as the ability of the software to function as per user requirements and of course no defects.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows the perceived impact of Agile methodologies on software quality from the practitioner's perspective.
codebook.notes: Retained based on Discussion-Agent justifications that emphasize Agile's nuanced and broad impact on quality.
